title: Sink or Float Lab
shareTitle: Sink or Float Lab 🫙 — Predict, Drop, Discover
description: Guess what each object will do, drop it into a big jar of real water yourself, and watch a live buoyancy simulation answer. Fifty-four everyday objects with honest, repeatable densities — every round a fresh, balanced set of three floaters and three sinkers — stamped into your own field journal. For ages 5–6.
learningGoals: Make a prediction, test it, and observe the result — the scientific method, felt physically
Discover that whether something floats depends on what it is made of, not how big it is
Notice degrees of floating and sinking: an apple rides deep, a leaf sits on top, an egg sinks slowly
Record an observation and read it back from a picture journal
interactionModel: Tap a pictorial sink-or-float guess badge, then drag (or tap) the object over the jar and let go — the release point is where it really falls into a live water simulation.
feedbackModel: The water is the teacher: splash, bobbing float or bubbling descent, then a spoken result and a journal stamp. A correct prediction is praised; a missed one is framed as a surprise with identical warmth and celebration. Wrong input or idling gets a gentle wiggle plus one spoken nudge, never an error.

modes.title: Water Playground
modes.skill: open observation of what water does

credits: Water simulation, glass jar and object placeholders drawn in code (shared/js/stage/water.js). Field Journal art plates in production on the local GenAI API. Built with Claude Code for QLOBE Kids.
